macros.title: Four-man rush
macros.note: Existing disguise package versus a dedicated stunt package. The original remains available.

before.name: MUDDY WATER
before.goal: Change the picture without opening an easy outlet.
before.user: Take away the first route entering your assignment and make the QB reset his read.
before.risk: Extra blitzers can give a patient QB a faster answer.
before.use: Keep sound coverage while changing the pre-snap picture.

settings.why: Show two high safeties before the snap.
settings.risk: Disguise does not change the called coverage; check alignment after motion.

atLine.why: Change the rush paths without adding a fifth rusher.
atLine.when: Optional only with four rushing defensive linemen; do not apply to a three-man front or a call dropping a lineman.

before.callout: Keep sound coverage while changing the pre-snap picture.

after.name: SPREAD TEXAS
after.goal: Create a different rush path without adding a blitzer.
after.user: Cover your assignment through the first read; watch the QB escape without abandoning a receiver.
after.risk: A stunt can lose rush-lane spacing. Four linemen do not guarantee pressure.
after.use: Four rushing defensive linemen; inspect the rush paths before applying. Four total rushers alone is not enough.

settings.why: Widen the line to meet the outside blocking surface.
settings.risk: An inside crease or cutback can open. Keep an inside defender home.

settings.why: Exchange rush lanes with the existing line.
settings.risk: Protection can pick this up; losing an edge can invite a rollout.
settings.when: Confirm four rushing linemen and remove conflicting contain assignments.

atLine.why: Tell the defense to anticipate the throw.
atLine.when: Only when a pass is highly likely; draws and handoffs punish the guess.

after.callout: Four rushing defensive linemen; inspect the rush paths before applying. Four total rushers alone is not enough.

macros.title: Rollout against a stunt
macros.note: Dedicated opposite-side pairing; do not combine the two packages.

before.name: PLASTER KIT
before.goal: Keep the quarterback in the pocket and protect the late throw.
before.user: With an underneath assignment, watch the step-up lane without abandoning a receiver still in your area.
before.risk: Contain does not close the middle or guarantee a sack.
before.use: At least two rushers; leave coverage behind the contain.

settings.why: Keep the outside rush from running past the quarterback.
settings.risk: The QB can still step up or run through the middle.

atLine.why: Choose a fast underneath defender, not a deep safety. You lose that defender’s original zone or man assignment.
atLine.when: Only if the remaining defense still covers every receiver.

before.callout: At least two rushers; leave coverage behind the contain.

after.name: STUNT & CONTAIN
after.goal: Keep the preferred escape edge while changing the opposite rush.
after.user: Read the rollout direction on the field. Keep coverage on the late throw.
after.risk: Contain and a stunt on the same edge can overwrite one another; inspect the final paths.
after.use: A compatible four-man rush front, with a clear rollout tendency to one side.

settings.why: Widen the line to meet the outside blocking surface.
settings.risk: An inside crease or cutback can open. Keep an inside defender home.
settings.when: Confirm the front supports the two-man stunt; total rusher count does not identify the linemen.

atLine.value: Left Tex 2-Man + Right Contain, or Right Tex 2-Man + Left Contain
atLine.why: Contain the observed escape side; stunt the opposite side.
atLine.when: Choose one pair after seeing the formation. Verify both paths; do not add Both Contain over the stunt.

after.callout: A compatible four-man rush front, with a clear rollout tendency to one side.

macros.title: Inside releases against man
macros.note: A new Cover 2 Man option; the broader crossers package remains.

before.name: MESH CRUSH
before.goal: Make the quarterback throw around the middle defender.
before.user: Wall the first crosser entering your zone. Pass it off instead of chasing it across the field.
before.risk: A dig behind the shallow crosser can open the next window.
before.use: Crossing routes; keep an underneath defender in the middle.

settings.why: Make the inside release harder to win.
settings.risk: Outside breaks have more room.

atLine.why: Anticipate the inside break after the opponent repeats it.
atLine.when: Optional after a clear tendency; an outside break punishes the guess.

before.callout: Crossing routes; keep an underneath defender in the middle.

after.name: PRESS INSIDE
after.goal: Contest repeated inside releases with two-high man help.
after.user: Stay with your assigned receiver or deep area; an RB release still belongs to his man defender.
after.risk: Outside breaks, lost presses and double moves can win. Route commit is a tendency guess.
after.use: Cover 2 Man, with two deep helpers and corners able to contest the release.

settings.why: Disrupt the release before the route develops.
settings.risk: A lost press can become a deep shot.
settings.when: Use with man coverage, deep help and corners who can win the matchup.

settings.why: Make the inside release harder to win.
settings.risk: Outside breaks have more room.

atLine.why: Anticipate the inside break after the opponent repeats it.
atLine.when: Optional after a clear tendency; an outside break punishes the guess.

after.callout: Cover 2 Man, with two deep helpers and corners able to contest the release.

macros.title: Inside the 10
macros.note: New package with eight setup controls and two manual role changes. A generic red-zone label does not qualify.

before.name: CARD COUNTER
before.goal: Defend the goal line and the immediate throw.
before.user: Check the QB run, then protect your receiver or zone through the first route break.
before.risk: Rub routes and sprint-outs can force a fast choice.
before.use: Spot-drop zone at the goal line with a separate QB-run defender.

settings.why: Keep hook defenders close to the quick middle throw.
settings.risk: Routes behind the hook become easier.
settings.when: Spot-drop zone in short yardage only; do not use for long yardage.

settings.why: Keep the outside rush from running past the quarterback.
settings.risk: The QB can still step up or run through the middle.

before.callout: Spot-drop zone at the goal line with a separate QB-run defender.

after.name: INSIDE TEN
after.goal: Contest immediate scores in a compressed field.
after.user: Finish the full setup before the snap. Stay responsible for your receiver or zone, especially the back corner.
after.risk: This is a manually altered call. Aggressive reactions can expose routes behind them; use a simpler call if there is no setup time.
after.use: Tampa 2 inside the opponent’s 10-yard line only. Reassign the actual outside corners and deep safeties after checking play art.

settings.why: Bring the defensive line closer to the inside run lanes.
settings.risk: The edge is easier to reach; do not chase an outside run with this package.

settings.why: Keep the outside rush from running past the quarterback.
settings.risk: The QB can still step up or run through the middle.

settings.why: Clear rush-lane exchanges before containing both edges.
settings.risk: Removing the stunt changes how the rush attacks protection.

settings.why: Make the read defender favor the QB keep.
settings.risk: The inside defenders still have to stop the handoff.

settings.why: Favor the quarterback on the read.
settings.risk: Interior defenders still need to handle the handoff.

settings.why: Set the flat-drop limit for this compressed field.
settings.risk: A drop depth does not guarantee coverage of the back corner.
settings.when: Inside the 10, after assigning the hard flats.

settings.why: Keep hook defenders close to the quick middle throw.
settings.risk: Routes behind the hook become easier.
settings.when: Spot-drop zone in short yardage only; do not use for long yardage.

settings.why: Challenge the immediate scoring throw.
settings.risk: Routes behind the first break remain dangerous.
settings.when: Only inside the 10 with the manual coverage changes completed.

atLine.why: Keep a short outside defender beneath each safety.
atLine.when: Identify the outside corners; never assume depth-chart numbers tell you their on-field roles.

atLine.why: Keep both safeties covering the end zone.
atLine.when: Confirm both deep safety roles. This changes the stock call; protect the back corners yourself from your assignment.

after.callout: Tampa 2 inside the opponent’s 10-yard line only. Reassign the actual outside corners and deep safeties after checking play art.

macros.title: Protecting a late lead
macros.note: New touchdown-prevention package. The original sideline plan still serves a different goal.

before.name: CLOCK COP
before.goal: Defend the line to gain and the sideline catch.
before.user: Keep routes in front of you and tackle inbounds when possible.
before.risk: Conceding short throws can still put the offense in winning field-goal range.
before.use: Protect the sideline while still defending the first-down line.

settings.why: Make the outside release harder to win.
settings.risk: Slants and digs have more room.

settings.why: Favor staying above the receiver instead of jumping the first break.
settings.risk: Short completions are easier.

before.callout: Protect the sideline while still defending the first-down line.

after.name: PROTECT THE LEAD
after.goal: Keep the touchdown in front of the defense.
after.user: Carry the seam through your zone and rally to the throw. Keep track of clock and field-goal range.
after.risk: Short catches, seams and extended plays still need defending. A field-goal stop needs a different plan.
after.use: Spot-drop Tampa 2 or Cover 3 Sky when preventing a quick touchdown is the goal. Switch plans if a field goal can beat you.

settings.why: Prioritize routes developing downfield.
settings.risk: Short completions can still create field-goal range.

settings.why: Keep defenders in their zone assignments on extended plays.
settings.risk: Receivers may find space as the quarterback buys time.

settings.why: Make the read defender favor the QB keep.
settings.risk: The inside defenders still have to stop the handoff.

settings.why: Leave the read defender focused on the quarterback.
settings.risk: The interior must handle the handoff.

settings.why: Give the receiver cushion instead of risking a lost press.
settings.risk: Hitches and quick outs can be easy catches.

atLine.value: Verify cloud flats on both sides
atLine.why: Leave the deep coverage intact while checking the outside zones.
atLine.when: On Cover 3 Sky, change only the flat defenders. Check the actual Tampa 2 variant rather than assuming its zones.

atLine.value: Zone It for the applicable family and receiver alignment
atLine.why: Keep a straight-zone plan if a matching check is active.
atLine.when: Apply only to the relevant check; do not change unrelated coverage families.

after.callout: Spot-drop Tampa 2 or Cover 3 Sky when preventing a quick touchdown is the goal. Switch plans if a field goal can beat you.

macros.title: Layering the sideline
macros.note: The core 25/5 layering already existed. The new entry makes Tampa 2 prerequisites and opposite-side effects explicit.

before.name: HOLE PLUG
before.goal: Keep the corner route capped while the flat defender handles the hitch.
before.user: Gain depth under the corner from your assigned zone; rally to the hitch after the throw.
before.risk: One defender cannot cover the hitch and corner at the same time.
before.use: Spot-drop Cover 2/Tampa 2 with separate defenders for hitch and corner.

settings.why: Start a cloud flat deeper under the corner route.
settings.risk: This defender cannot also take the quick flat.
settings.when: Use cloud flats with a separate underneath defender on the attacked side; tune to the actual route depth.

settings.why: Give the deeper flat defender a separate short-route helper.
settings.risk: That helper leaves less room to defend the middle.
settings.when: Pair with the deeper cloud flat; check which underneath defender you reassign.

atLine.value: Curl Flat under the cloud flat
atLine.why: Use a separate underneath defender on the attacked side; keep the deep safety in coverage.
atLine.when: Start with spot-drop Cover 2/Tampa 2 and identify both defenders in the play art.

before.callout: Spot-drop Cover 2/Tampa 2 with separate defenders for hitch and corner.

after.name: TAMPA MABLE
after.goal: Give short and deeper sideline routes different defenders.
after.user: Protect the inside space left by the reassigned underneath helper.
after.risk: Global drops affect both sides. Layering one sideline can weaken the middle or the opposite side.
after.use: Tampa 2 with a cloud flat and a separate underneath helper on the attacked side. Start with Nickel Over and inspect the roles.

settings.why: Start a cloud flat deeper under the corner route.
settings.risk: This defender cannot also take the quick flat.
settings.when: Use cloud flats with a separate underneath defender on the attacked side; tune to the actual route depth.

settings.why: Give the deeper flat defender a separate short-route helper.
settings.risk: That helper leaves less room to defend the middle.
settings.when: Pair with the deeper cloud flat; check which underneath defender you reassign.

atLine.value: Curl Flat under the cloud flat
atLine.why: Use a separate underneath defender on the attacked side; keep the deep safety in coverage.
atLine.when: Start with spot-drop Cover 2/Tampa 2 and identify both defenders in the play art.

atLine.value: Check the other flat after changing global drop depths
atLine.why: The global Flats setting also affects the opposite flat defender.
atLine.when: Keep deep help there. Use two underneath helpers only when both exist; do not assume every dime package has two suitable slots.

after.callout: Tampa 2 with a cloud flat and a separate underneath helper on the attacked side. Start with Nickel Over and inspect the roles.

adjustments.title: Mobile QB with RPO and pitch

objective.label: Stay balanced
objective.text: Use the selected call as drawn, then make one change only when the scouting report points to a clear problem.

settings.why: Keep the outermost rushers outside the quarterback and force him to step up into traffic.
settings.tradeoff: Contain protects the edge, not the middle. The user must still see the step-up or draw.

tools.why: Present one-high before rotating to the selected two-high call after the snap.
tools.tradeoff: Do not sacrifice getting lined up just to disguise the call.

tools.why: Use after the attached RPO throw repeatedly beats your conflict defender; this tells him to favor pass coverage.
tools.tradeoff: The run gap receives less help. If the offense starts handing it off, return to Balanced.

preset.why: Use when the quarterback keeps escaping or extending pass plays.
preset.tradeoff: Turn it off if the quarterback stays in the pocket and attacks the extra attention around him.

alerts.when: The quarterback stays in the pocket
alerts.action: If you applied QB Contain, reset the play before returning to its normal rush. Reapply any other adjustments you still need.

userKey.title: Slow-play the conflict
userKey.text: Stay square through the mesh. Force the handoff or throw, then commit—chasing too early gives the quarterback the answer.
